# Appendix E: Exact agenda-stage correspondences and comparisons {-}

## E.1 Agenda-stage contract {-}

Fix
\[
\begin{gathered}
\mathbf d=(N,m,q,k,c,\beta,o_0,o_1,\bar y,\mathcal Y,\nu),\\
m=N-1\geq3,\quad q=\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1,\quad
k=q-1,\quad c=m-k,\\
0<\beta<1,\quad 0<o_0<o_1<1,\quad
o_1\leq\bar y\leq1,\quad \nu\in[0,1].
\end{gathered}
\]
At date \(A\), after observing its type, \(H\) proposes
\[
s^A=(z_H,(x_j)_{j\in W})\in\mathcal Y,\qquad
\mathcal Y=\{s^A:z_H\geq0,\ x_j\geq0,\
z_H+\textstyle\sum_jx_j\leq1\}.
\]
The proposal counts as \(H\)'s affirmative vote. Weak states vote
simultaneously and in pure strategies. Majority requires \(k\) affirmative
weak votes; unanimity requires all \(m\). Passage implements the package at
date \(A\). Rejection enters the corresponding frozen Round-1 continuation,
whose native payoff is multiplied by \(\beta\) exactly once.

A rejected public history includes the rule, proposal, proposer, full ballot,
outcome, and posterior. Its continuation selector is total, public, Borel,
common to types compatible with the history, and returns one complete frozen
Round-1 equilibrium record. A record binds strategies, beliefs, recognition
lotteries, ballots, payoffs, and outcomes. No scalar continuation payoff may
replace it.

For an interior prior, the equilibrium proposal laws of the two types are
Borel measures \(\sigma_0,\sigma_1\). At every disciplined proposal, Bayes'
rule determines the posterior from their local likelihood ratio. At
undisciplined proposals, the M/S/B restriction fixes the posterior to
\[
p=b_\rho(\nu)=\frac{\nu\rho}{1-\nu+\nu\rho},
\qquad \rho\in[0,\infty].
\]
The extended-real boundary conventions are
\[
b_0(\nu)=0,\qquad b_\infty(\nu)=1
\]
for an interior prior. The endpoints preserve prior support: \(p=\nu\)
everywhere, \(\eta=(*,\nu)\), and \(\rho\) is irrelevant. Voting follows the
same as-if-pivotal comparison and
indifference-to-yes convention as the baseline.

## E.2 Complete private-majority correspondence {-}

For each posterior \(p\) and a fixed anonymous Markov continuation selection
\(\chi\), let \(A_\chi(p)\) be \(H\)'s best payoff from a proposal that
passes and let \(D_{\chi\theta}(p)\) be type \(\theta\)'s payoff from
rejection, both at date \(A\). Define
\[
A_p:=A_\chi(p),\qquad D_{\theta p}:=D_{\chi\theta}(p),
\qquad p\in[0,1],
\]
so that \(A_\nu,A_0,A_1\) and
\(D_{0\nu},D_{1\nu},D_{00},D_{01},D_{10},D_{11}\) denote evaluations of
these same functions at the displayed posterior. Also define
\[
O_\theta(\rho)
=\max\{A_\chi(b_\rho(\nu)),D_{\chi\theta}(b_\rho(\nu))\}.
\]
The following conditions are necessary and sufficient for every interior
pure equilibrium class:

\begin{longtable}{p{0.22\linewidth}p{0.70\linewidth}}
\caption{Pure private-majority classes at the agenda stage}\label{tab:ampure}\\
\toprule
Class & Necessary and sufficient condition and linked type payoff \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Class & Necessary and sufficient condition and linked type payoff \\
\midrule
\endhead
Pooling agreement &
\(O_1(\rho)\leq A_\nu\), with any
\(z\in[O_1(\rho),A_\nu]\); linked payoff \((z,z)\) \\
Pooling delay &
\(D_{0\nu}\geq O_0(\rho)\) and
\(D_{1\nu}\geq O_1(\rho)\); linked payoff
\((D_{0\nu},D_{1\nu})\) \\
Separating agreement--agreement &
\(O_1(\rho)\leq\min\{A_0,A_1\}\), with any
\(z\in[O_1(\rho),\min\{A_0,A_1\}]\); linked payoff \((z,z)\) \\
Low agreement, high delay &
\(D_{11}\geq O_1(\rho)\) and
\(\max\{D_{01},O_0(\rho)\}\leq\min\{A_0,D_{11}\}\); linked payoff
\[
(z,D_{11}),\qquad
z\in[\max\{D_{01},O_0(\rho)\},\min\{A_0,D_{11}\}]
\] \\
Low delay, high agreement & Impossible; linked payoff \(\varnothing\) \\
Separating delay--delay &
\(D_{00}\geq D_{01}\), \(D_{11}\geq D_{10}\),
\(D_{00}\geq O_0(\rho)\), and \(D_{11}\geq O_1(\rho)\); linked payoff
\((D_{00},D_{11})\) \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

These classes preserve proposals and messages even when their payoffs
coincide. Separating agreement at the same \(z\) is separation in messages at
indifference, not pooling. The off-path feasibility set for \(\rho\) can be
disconnected because the frozen majority continuation changes branches; no
single cutoff substitutes for the table.

For mixed strategies, a complete reduced record is
\[
R_M=(\rho,p,\sigma_0,\sigma_1,\lambda,\pi,\chi,
a,u_0,u_1).
\]
It retains the public proposal law \(\lambda\), posterior map \(\pi\),
continuation selection \(\chi\), ballot map \(a\), and both type payoffs.
Bayes holds pointwise on the disciplined support, every weak vote satisfies
the pivotal comparison at every proposal, and each type's proposal law is
supported on its global best responses. This criterion is necessary and
sufficient; arbitrary Borel mixtures and atomless supports are included.

At \(\nu\in\{0,1\}\), the posterior is fixed at the endpoint. With
\[
M_\theta=\max\{A_\nu,D_{\theta\nu}\},
\]
each type's Borel proposal law may be any probability measure supported on
its argmax. The probability-zero type remains part of the linked record.
For every admissible primitive and prior, at least one majority PBE exists
for some \(\rho\); this does not assert existence at every fixed \(\rho\).

## E.3 Complete private-unanimity correspondence {-}

Define
\[
\nu^*=\frac{o_1-o_0}{1-o_0},\quad
\ell=\beta o_0,\quad h=\beta o_1,\quad
d_0=\beta^2o_0,\quad d_H=\beta^2o_1,
\]
\[
\begin{gathered}
a=\frac{\beta(1-\ell)}m,\qquad
b=\frac{\beta(1-h)}m,\\
z_L=1-\beta+\beta^2o_0,\qquad
z_H=1-\beta+\beta^2o_1,\qquad
\Delta_U=z_L-d_H.
\end{gathered}
\]
Thus \(0<b<a\), \(d_0<d_H\), and the two proposal primitives are
\[
y_L=(z_L,a,\ldots,a),\qquad
y_H=(z_H,b,\ldots,b).
\]
At posterior zero, every weak state accepts exactly when \(x_j\geq a\); at a
high posterior, it accepts exactly when \(x_j\geq b\). Equality passes by
\(T^Y\). The only continuation posteriors admitted by the frozen unanimity
continuation are
\[
\mathcal D_C=\{0\}\cup(\nu^*,1].
\]
Rejection pays type 1 \(d_H\) at every admissible posterior; it pays type 0
\(d_0\) at posterior zero and \(d_H\) at a high posterior.

A complete unanimity member is the indivisible binder
\[
R_U=(\sigma_0,\sigma_1,\mu,p,\widehat\kappa_U,v,Q,
     \Gamma_0,\Gamma_1).
\]
Here \(\sigma_\theta\) is a Borel proposal law,
\(\bar\sigma=(1-\nu)\sigma_0+\nu\sigma_1\), \(\mu\) is the public posterior,
and \(p=\nu_{\mathrm{off}}\in\mathcal D_C\) is its single value at every
undisciplined proposal. The selector \(\widehat\kappa_U\) returns a complete
literal frozen continuation member at the same posterior, \(v\) is the full
pure ballot map, and \(Q_\theta(y)\) is the literal terminal law induced by
passage or by that continuation. Finally, \(\Gamma_\theta\) is the realized
pushforward law of the joint record
\[
(y,\mu(y),v(y),\text{pass/reject},\widehat\kappa_U,
  Q_\theta(y),\text{date-}A\text{ payoffs}).
\]
The local Bayes limit must exist at every disciplined proposal, including
zero-mass limit points, and must lie in \(\mathcal D_C\). At each such point,
and at every undisciplined point evaluated with \(p\), neither type may obtain
a profitable proposal deviation. These pointwise restrictions, the ballot
map, the literal continuation, and both realized laws are part of the same
binder and cannot be recombined across members.

The full interior correspondence is generated by the following two families.

**Low-posterior family \(\mathrm{AU\mbox{-}MSB\mbox{-}L}\).** Its exact
domain is
\[
0<\nu<1,\qquad \Delta_U\geq0,\qquad p=0.
\]
Choose Borel laws satisfying all of the following:

1. \(\sigma_0(\{y_L\})=\alpha_L>0\) and
   \(\sigma_1(\{y_L\})=0\);
2. outside \(y_L\), \(\mu(y)>\nu^*\)
   \(\bar\sigma\)-almost surely;
3. each used proposal outside \(y_L\) either passes with \(H\)'s share
   \(z_L\), or, only when \(\Delta_U=0\), rejects and pays \(d_H=z_L\);
4. every disciplined proposal, including every zero-mass limit point, gives
   each type a deviation payoff no larger than \(z_L\); every undisciplined
   proposal satisfies the same inequality under posterior zero.

Every accepted high-posterior signal therefore belongs to
\[
\mathcal K_L=\{y\in\mathcal Y:z=z_L,\ \min_jx_j\geq b\}.
\]
The laws may be asymmetric, discrete, semi-pooling, mixed, or atomless. A
pure witness has type 0 propose \(y_L\) and type 1 propose
\(y_S=(z_L,b,\ldots,b)\). Every member has linked payoff
\((z_L,z_L)\). If \(\Delta_U>0\), agreement occurs with probability one for
both types; if \(\Delta_U=0\), high-posterior rejected signals may carry mass.
The weak-state payoff attached to the same member is \(x_j\) after passage,
\(a\) after rejection at \((\mu,\theta)=(0,0)\), zero after rejection at
\((0,1)\), and \(b\) after rejection at any high posterior.

**High-posterior family \(\mathrm{AU\mbox{-}MSB\mbox{-}H}\).** Its necessary
prior domain is \(\nu^*<\nu<1\). When \(p=0\), choose any
\[
u\in[u_{\min},z_H],\qquad u_{\min}=\max\{z_L,d_H\},
\]
and Borel laws such that: \(\mu>\nu^*\)
\(\bar\sigma\)-almost surely; the local admissible Bayes limit exists at
every disciplined point; every used accepted proposal lies in
\[
\mathcal K_H(u)=\{y\in\mathcal Y:z=u,\ \min_jx_j\geq b\};
\]
used rejected proposals occur only when \(u=d_H\); every disciplined
deviation gives each type at most \(u\); and every undisciplined deviation,
evaluated at posterior zero, also gives at most \(u\). The linked payoff is
\((u,u)\). If \(u>d_H\), agreement has probability one for each type; if
\(u=d_H\), each type may mix accepted proposals with \(z=d_H\) and rejected
high-posterior proposals. A pure pooling witness for every \(u\) is
\[
y(u)=\left(u,\frac{1-u}{m},\ldots,\frac{1-u}{m}\right),qquad
\sigma_0=\sigma_1=\delta_{y(u)},\qquad \mu(y(u))=\nu.
\]
When \(p\in(\nu^*,1]\), the only current proposal laws are
\(\sigma_0=\sigma_1=\delta_{y_H}\), with \(\mu(y_H)=\nu\) and payoff
\((z_H,z_H)\); multiplicity survives only in \(p\) and the complete literal
continuation binder. When \(p\in(0,\nu^*]\), the correspondence is empty.
For \(\nu^*<\nu<1\) and \(p=0\), the high-posterior family always exists,
and the low-posterior family is additionally present exactly when
\(\Delta_U\geq0\). For \(0<\nu\leq\nu^*\), equilibrium exists exactly when
\(\Delta_U\geq0\) and consists only of the low-posterior family. There is no
third interior family.

The endpoints are complete Borel strategy correspondences, not one-sided
limits. At \(\nu=0\), support preservation fixes \(\mu(y)=p=0\) everywhere,
\(\sigma_0=\delta_{y_L}\), and the counterfactual high-type law is
\[
\begin{cases}
\delta_{y_L},&\Delta_U>0,\\
\text{any Borel law supported on }\{y_L\}\cup\mathcal R_L,
 &\Delta_U=0,\\
\text{any Borel law supported on }\mathcal R_L,&\Delta_U<0,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\mathcal R_L=\{y\in\mathcal Y:\min_jx_j<a\}.
\]
The linked payoff is
\((z_L,\max\{z_L,d_H\})\), and type 0 agrees immediately with probability
one. At \(\nu=1\), support preservation fixes \(\mu(y)=p=1\) everywhere and
\(\sigma_0=\sigma_1=\delta_{y_H}\), including the probability-zero type's
strategy, with linked payoff
\[
V_U^{A,01}=(z_H,z_H).
\]

Consequently, the payoff image of the complete correspondence is
\[
V_U^{A,01}=
\begin{cases}
(z_L,\max\{z_L,d_H\}),&\nu=0,\\
(z_L,z_L),&0<\nu\leq\nu^*,\ \Delta_U\geq0,\ p=0,\\
\{(u,u):u\in[u_{\min},z_H]\},&\nu^*<\nu<1,\ p=0,\\
(z_H,z_H),&\nu^*<\nu<1,\ p\in(\nu^*,1],\\
(z_H,z_H),&\nu=1,\\
\varnothing,&\text{all remaining fibers}.
\end{cases}
\]
This display is only an image: it neither replaces the binder nor converts
an interval of linked vectors into a Cartesian product.

For the two-layer representation, let \(Z_U\) be the compact realized-record
space containing the named proposal and ballot coordinates, the realized
posterior, pass/reject, the literal continuation-cell identity, and the
terminal allocation and payoff record. Then
\[
\Gamma_\theta^{U,R_U}
=\operatorname{Law}_\theta
 (y,\mu(y),v(y),\text{pass/reject},\xi_U,\omega_T)
\in\mathcal P(Z_U).
\]
Under a common permutation \(g\) of weak-state names, let \(T_g\) relabel
every named weak-state coordinate and let \(\Lambda_x\) code the diagonal
orbit of \(x=(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\). For interior priors,
\[
\operatorname{Sig}^{ex}_U(R_U)=(\rho,p,\Lambda_x),\qquad
\operatorname{Sum}^{econ}_U(R_U)
=(\rho,p,(q_U)_\#\Gamma_0,(q_U)_\#\Gamma_1),
\]
with endpoint forms \((*,\nu,\Lambda_x)\) and
\((*,\nu,(q_U)_\#\Gamma_0,(q_U)_\#\Gamma_1)\). The exact signature preserves
the diagonal orbit of realized laws and their relevant realized identities;
the economic layer removes names record by record. Neither layer contains
the full off-path functions. Formal-identity and realized-law operations use
the exact signature; any operation that depends on off-path beliefs,
strategies, supports, messages, or continuation plans must instead consume
the underlying complete binder. No Reynolds average is treated as an
equilibrium representative, and every \texttt{none} cell above remains empty
in both layers.

## E.4 Exact same-fiber institutional comparison {-}

Let \(\mathcal B_M(\mathbf d,\eta)\) and
\(\mathcal B_U(\mathbf d,\eta)\) be the full
correspondences just described. The admissible comparison set is
\[
\mathcal J_{AC}^{\mathrm{bind}}(\mathbf d,\eta)
=\mathcal B_M(\mathbf d,\eta)
 \times_{(\mathbf d,\eta)}\mathcal B_U(\mathbf d,\eta).
\]
This product requires identical primitives and the same fiber, but it imposes
no common proposal, continuation realization, or cross-world randomization.
The exact linked type-payoff contrast is
\[
\mathcal D_{01}(\mathbf d,\eta)
=\{u-m:u\in V_U^{A,01}(\mathbf d,\eta),\
             m\in V_M^{A,01}(\mathbf d,\eta)\}.
\]
It is a difference of complete vectors. The ex ante image is
\[
\mathcal D_E(\mathbf d,\eta)
=\{(1-\nu)x_0+\nu x_1:
  (x_0,x_1)\in\mathcal D_{01}(\mathbf d,\eta)\}.
\]
It is generally not equal to the sum of independently chosen marginal
images. Dominance claims are setwise: unanimity dominates in a coordinate
only when every member has positive sign; majority dominates only when every
member has negative sign. A crossing set is selection dependent. An empty
fiber has classification \texttt{none}, not sign zero.

## E.5 The sufficient majority-advantage region {-}

Every majority binder satisfies
\[
V_M^{A,\theta}\geq\max\{Z_E,\beta^2o_\theta\},
\qquad Z_E=1-\frac{k\beta}{m},
\]
while every unanimity binder satisfies
\[
V_U^{A,\theta}\leq z_H=1-\beta+\beta^2o_1.
\]
Therefore
\[
Z_E-z_H
=\beta\left(\frac{c}{m}-\beta o_1\right)=g_{T5}.
\]
If \(\beta o_1<c/m\), then \(g_{T5}>0\) and every comparable member
satisfies
\[
V_M^{A,\theta}-V_U^{A,\theta}\geq g_{T5}>0
\]
for \(\theta=0,1\) and ex ante. Equality yields weak majority advantage.
This proves sufficiency only.

The condition is not necessary. With
\[
N=5,\ m=4,\ k=2,\ c=2,\ \beta=.9,
o_0=.5,\ o_1=.6,\ \bar y=.8,\ \nu=0,
\]
we have \(c/m=.5\) and \(\beta o_1=.54>.5\), so the condition fails.
Nevertheless \(Z_E=.55\), \(z_L=.505\), and \(d_H=.486\); hence every
majority binder strictly exceeds the endpoint unanimity vector
\((.505,.505)\).

The excluded fraction is
\[
\frac{c}{m}=
\begin{cases}
1/2,&N\text{ odd},\\[3pt]
(N-2)/(2(N-1)),&N\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
\]
In an existing low-prior cell, the weaker local condition
\(\beta o_0<c/m\) gives the margin
\(g_0=\beta(c/m-\beta o_0)\). At \(\nu=0\), that condition guarantees only
the ex ante conclusion unless the full counterfactual type vector is used.

## E.6 Public-majority PBE classes {-}

For public \(o\leq1/m\), each weak vote costs
\[
r_M(o)=\frac{\beta(1-\beta o)}{m}.
\]
Every optimal proposal pays exactly \(r_M(o)\) to exactly \(k\) weak states,
pays zero to the rest, and leaves
\[
P_I(o)=1-\frac{k\beta(1-\beta o)}{m}
\]
to \(H\). Every probability measure over these minimal coalitions is a PBE
proposal lottery. Passage strictly dominates the delayed payoff
\(\beta^2o\).

For \(o>1/m\), every purchased weak vote costs \(\beta/m\), so passage
leaves \(Z_E\) and rejection yields \(\beta o\). Thus:
\[
\begin{array}{rcl}
1/m<o<\tau_M&:&\text{every PBE passes through a minimal coalition},\\
o=\tau_M&:&\text{every linked mixture of minimal passage and delay is allowed},\\
o>\tau_M&:&\text{every PBE deliberately delays}.
\end{array}
\]
At the tie, the same mixture weight binds the proposal, result, and agreement
probability. The public payoff is always the singleton
\[
h_M(o)=
\begin{cases}
P_I(o),&o\leq1/m,\\
\max\{Z_E,\beta o\},&o>1/m.
\end{cases}
\]

## E.7 Public-unanimity PBE {-}

Every weak vote costs
\[
r_U(o)=\frac{\beta(1-\beta o)}{m}.
\]
The unique optimal on-path proposal pays this amount to all \(m\) weak
states and leaves
\[
h_U(o)=1-\beta+\beta^2o
\]
to \(H\). Rejection yields \(\beta^2o\), so passage is strictly better by
\(1-\beta\). Agreement is immediate and payoff-determined for every public
type; no majority-style delay is imported into this rule.

## E.8 The public gap {-}

Subtracting E.7 from E.6 gives
\[
G(o)=
\begin{cases}
\beta(c/m)(1-\beta o),&o\leq1/m,\\
\beta(c/m-\beta o),&o>1/m,\ \beta o\leq Z_E,\\
(1-\beta)(\beta o-1),&o>1/m,\ \beta o\geq Z_E.
\end{cases}
\]
Continuity holds at \(\beta o=Z_E\). For \(o>1/m\),
\[
\operatorname{sgn}G(o)=\operatorname{sgn}(c/m-\beta o).
\]
At \(o=1/m\), the first branch applies because the frozen no-agenda
continuation includes \(H\) at equality. This special selection also matters
for the direct agenda effect in E.12.

## E.9 Exact informational-rent translations {-}

For every complete private binder,
\[
RI_g^{A,01}
=V_g^{A,01}-(h_g(o_0),h_g(o_1)).
\]
This fixed-vector translation preserves every atom, mixture, and linked type
coordinate. The exact unanimity cells are:

\begin{longtable}{p{0.37\linewidth}p{0.37\linewidth}p{0.17\linewidth}}
\caption{Unanimity informational rent with hegemonic agenda}\label{tab:auri}\\
\toprule
Fiber & \(RI_U^{A,01}\) & Ex ante image \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Fiber & \(RI_U^{A,01}\) & Ex ante image \\
\midrule
\endhead
\(\nu=0\) &
\((0,\max\{z_L,d_H\}-z_H)\) & \(0\) \\
\(0<\nu\leq\nu^*\), \(\Delta_U\geq0\), \(p=0\) &
\((0,-(z_H-z_L))\) & \(-\nu(z_H-z_L)\) \\
Other low-prior fibers & \(\varnothing\) & \(\varnothing\) \\
\(\nu^*<\nu<1\), \(p=0\) &
\(\{(u-z_L,u-z_H):u\in[u_{\min},z_H]\}\) &
\([u_{\min}-z_E(\nu),z_H-z_E(\nu)]\) \\
\(\nu^*<\nu<1\), \(p\in(\nu^*,1]\) &
\((z_H-z_L,0)\) & \((1-\nu)(z_H-z_L)\) \\
\(\nu^*<\nu<1\), \(p\in(0,\nu^*]\) &
\(\varnothing\) & \(\varnothing\) \\
\(\nu=1\) & \((z_H-z_L,0)\) & \(0\) \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

Here \(z_E(\nu)=(1-\nu)z_L+\nu z_H\). Every existing cell satisfies
\[
RI_U^{A,0}\geq0,\qquad RI_U^{A,1}\leq0,
\]
with at least one strict inequality. Majority rent is retained as the exact
translation of the full majority payoff correspondence; it has no imposed
global sign.

## E.10 Public power and information decomposition {-}

For every same-fiber member,
\[
\Delta RI_A^\theta
=RI_U^{A,\theta}-RI_M^{A,\theta}
=\delta_\theta+G(o_\theta),
\]
or equivalently
\[
\delta_\theta=-G(o_\theta)+\Delta RI_A^\theta.
\]
If \(G(o_0)>0\) and a private member has \(\delta_0>0\), then
\[
\Delta RI_A^0>G(o_0)>0
\]
for that member. Type incidence precedes ex ante aggregation:
\[
\delta_E=-G_E+\Delta RI_A^E,\quad
G_E=(1-\nu)G(o_0)+\nu G(o_1).
\]
Under the sufficient condition in E.5,
\[
\delta_\theta\leq-g_{T5},\qquad
\Delta RI_A^\theta\leq G(o_\theta)-g_{T5}.
\]
This bounds the informational difference relative to the amount required to
reverse majority's guaranteed private advantage; it does not assign a sign
to \(\Delta RI_A^\theta\).

The numerical member in Figure \ref{fig:agendagap} gives
\[
\Delta RI_A^0=.5480,\qquad
G(o_0)=.4095,\qquad
\delta_0=.1385.
\]
These linked values illustrate the identity; they do not calibrate the WTO or
select globally from either correspondence.

## E.11 Factorial design and identity {-}

At date \(A\), the four cells are
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
&N&A\\ \hline
\text{public type}&\beta h_g^{N,R1}(o_\theta)&h_g^A(o_\theta)\\
\text{private type}&\beta V_g^{N,R1,\theta}&V_g^{A,\theta}.
\end{array}
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_g^\theta&=h_g^A(o_\theta)-\beta h_g^{N,R1}(o_\theta),\\
T_g^\theta&=V_g^{A,\theta}-\beta V_g^{N,R1,\theta},\\
I_g^\theta&=RI_g^{A,\theta}-\beta RI_g^{N,R1,\theta}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Substituting \(V=h+RI\) in both arms yields, by type and ex ante,
\[
T_g=D_g+I_g.
\]
The factor \(\beta\) appears once because the no-agenda arm begins one date
later. The treatment combines an earlier opportunity with a mandatory
proposal. Redating Round 1 to date \(A\) in the control would define another
structural contrast.

## E.12 Direct agenda effects and their institutional difference {-}

The rule-specific public effects are
\[
D_U(o)=1-\beta
\]
and
\[
D_M(o)=
\begin{cases}
Z_E-(c/m)\beta^2o,&o\leq1/m,\\
Z_E-\beta o,&1/m<o<\tau_M,\\
0,&o\geq\tau_M.
\end{cases}
\]
The threshold satisfies \(\tau_M>1/m\), but it can be weakly above one, in
which case the last branch is empty in the admissible domain. At \(o=1/m\),
the first branch applies. The frozen continuation selection creates the jump
\[
D_M(1/m)-\lim_{o\downarrow1/m,\ o>1/m}D_M(o)
=\frac{\beta}{m}\left(1-\frac{c\beta}{m}\right)>0.
\]

With \(\Delta D(o)=D_U(o)-D_M(o)\),
\[
\Delta D(o)=
\begin{cases}
-\beta(c/m)(1-\beta o),&o\leq1/m,\\
\beta(o-c/m),&1/m<o\leq\tau_M,\\
1-\beta,&o\geq\tau_M.
\end{cases}
\]
The last two formulas coincide at \(\tau_M\). This branchwise statement is
the frozen result; no stronger global classification from the later external
consultation is promoted here.

## E.13 Total private agenda effects {-}

Under unanimity, the exact linked correspondence is
\[
T_U^{01}=
\begin{cases}
(1-\beta,\max\{\Delta_U,0\}),&\nu=0,\\
\varnothing,&0<\nu\leq\nu^*,\\
\{(u-d_H,u-d_H):u\in[u_{\min},z_H]\},
 &\nu^*<\nu<1,\ p=0,\\
\varnothing,&\nu^*<\nu<1,\ p\in(0,\nu^*],\\
(1-\beta,1-\beta),&\nu^*<\nu<1,\ p\in(\nu^*,1],\\
(1-\beta,1-\beta),&\nu=1.
\end{cases}
\]
In the low-prior interior, the no-agenda control is always empty; the agenda
treatment may exist or may also be empty. In the high-prior low-positive
off-path fiber, the control exists but the agenda treatment is empty. These
different missing arms both propagate to an empty \(T_U\).

Where both arms exist, every unanimity member weakly benefits both types and
the maximum gain is \(1-\beta\). At \(\nu=0\), the ex ante gain is
\(1-\beta\) even if the probability-zero high coordinate is zero.

For majority, retain the exact interaction correspondence:
\[
T_M^{01}=D_M^{01}+I_M^{01}.
\]
For each coordinate and member,
\[
\begin{array}{rcl}
T_M^\theta>0&\Longleftrightarrow&I_M^\theta>-D_M(o_\theta),\\
T_M^\theta=0&\Longleftrightarrow&I_M^\theta=-D_M(o_\theta),\\
T_M^\theta<0&\Longleftrightarrow&I_M^\theta<-D_M(o_\theta).
\end{array}
\]
No selection-free sign follows when the source correspondence crosses the
threshold. Across rules,
\[
\Delta T^\theta=\Delta D^\theta+\Delta I^\theta
\]
member by member in every complete product. A robust ranking requires the
entire admissible correspondence to lie on one side of
\(-\Delta D^\theta\).

## E.14 The diagonal contrast {-}

The diagonal comparison is
\[
Q_g^\theta
=h_g^A(o_\theta)-\beta V_g^{N,R1,\theta}
=D_g^\theta-\beta RI_g^{N,R1,\theta}.
\]
It compares public information with agenda against private information
without agenda, changing two factors at once. It is not a causal effect of
agenda or information alone.

Under unanimity,
\[
Q_U^{01}=
\begin{cases}
(1-\beta,1-\beta),&\nu=0,\\
\varnothing,&0<\nu\leq\nu^*,\\
(\Delta_U,1-\beta),&\nu^*<\nu\leq1.
\end{cases}
\]
The ex ante value in the high-prior region is
\[
Q_U^E=1-\beta-(1-\nu)\beta^2(o_1-o_0).
\]
Under majority,
\[
Q_M^{01}=D_M^{01}-\beta RI_M^{N,R1,01}
\]
is the exact image of the applicable linked no-agenda records and remains
set-valued where those records do. \(Q_U\) may exist where \(T_U\) is empty
because it does not use the private agenda arm.

# Appendix F: Factorization, interaction, and scope {-}

## F.1 Exact and economic layers {-}

For majority, the exact signature is
\[
\operatorname{Sig}^{ex}_M(R_M)
=(\rho,p,\Lambda_{(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)}),
\]
where \(\Lambda\) codes the diagonal relabeling orbit of the two complete
realized laws. Its economic summary is
\[
\operatorname{Sum}^{econ}_M(R_M)
=(\rho,p,(q_Z)_\#\Gamma_0,(q_Z)_\#\Gamma_1).
\]
Unanimity uses the analogous pair
\(\operatorname{Sig}^{ex}_U\) and \(\operatorname{Sum}^{econ}_U\).
The exact signature preserves the diagonal relabeling orbit of the realized
laws and the relevant identities inside those realized records. It does not
retain the complete off-path belief, strategy, support, message, or
continuation functions. Those functions remain only in the underlying
complete binder, and every off-path-sensitive operation must consume that
binder. The economic layer retains the anonymous realized laws needed for
payoffs, agreement, delay, and anonymous outcomes.

The institutional operator is first applied to complete binders. Only after
that product is formed do payoff and outcome maps factor measurably through
the economic summaries:
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{econ}}(R_M,R_U)
=\overline{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{econ}}
(\operatorname{Sum}^{econ}_M(R_M),
 \operatorname{Sum}^{econ}_U(R_U)).
\]
No Reynolds average is an equilibrium representative. Equality of summaries
does not identify named proposals, coalition lotteries, or off-path plans.

For coordinate \(r\in\{0,1,E\}\), the contrast envelope satisfies
\[
\inf\mathcal D_r=\inf U_r-\sup M_r,\qquad
\sup\mathcal D_r=\sup U_r-\inf M_r.
\]
The interval between these numbers is an interval hull, not necessarily an
attained set. Likewise, the outcome object is the ordered pair of marginal
laws
\[
\mathcal O_{AC}(\mathbf d,\eta)
=\left\{
  ((\bar\Gamma_M^0,\bar\Gamma_M^1),
   (\bar\Gamma_U^0,\bar\Gamma_U^1)):
  (R_M,R_U)\in
  \mathcal J_{AC}^{\mathrm{bind}}(\mathbf d,\eta)
 \right\}.
\]
It is not a joint counterfactual distribution. A common cross-world draw or
coordinate splicing would add a primitive absent from the model.

## F.2 Interaction with the no-agenda benchmark {-}

Let \(RI_g^{N,R1,01}\) be the native Round-1 rent vector from the no-agenda
benchmark. The exact interaction is the Minkowski difference of complete
linked records,
\[
I_g^{01}
=RI_g^{A,01}-\beta RI_g^{N,R1,01}.
\]
For majority, the applicable no-agenda records are the II, IX, and XX cells
in Table \ref{tab:rents}; no general sign is inferred.

Under unanimity:
\[
I_U^{01}=
\begin{cases}
(0,\max\{z_L,d_H\}-z_H),&\nu=0,\\
\varnothing,&0<\nu\leq\nu^*,\\
\{(u-z_H,u-z_H):u\in[u_{\min},z_H]\},
 &\nu^*<\nu<1,\ p=0,\\
(0,0),&\nu^*<\nu<1,\ p\in(\nu^*,1],\\
\varnothing,&\nu^*<\nu<1,\ p\in(0,\nu^*],\\
(0,0),&\nu=1.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus agenda weakly reduces unanimity's informational rent in every existing
high-prior fiber; the change is strict for both types exactly when
\(p=0\) and \(u<z_H\). At \(\nu=0\), only the probability-zero high
coordinate falls.

The institutional interaction is
\[
\Delta I^{01}
=\Delta RI_A^{01}-\beta\Delta RI_N^{R1,01}.
\]
It exists only when both exact sources exist. It remains set-valued whenever
either source does and is never assembled from independently chosen marginal
coordinates.

## F.3 Payoff dates, existence, and verification limits {-}

All agenda-game values arrive at date \(A\). Native no-agenda Round-1 values
are multiplied by \(\beta\) exactly once before comparison. Public agenda
payoffs, private agenda payoffs, agenda rents, and their institutional
contrasts receive no additional factor.

The existence rules are:

\begin{itemize}
\item every public agenda game has a PBE for both rules and types;
\item \(RI_g^A\) exists exactly where the private agenda source exists;
\item \(\Delta RI_A\) exists exactly where the same-fiber product exists;
\item \(I_g\) exists exactly where both its agenda and no-agenda rent sources
exist;
\item \(\Delta I\), \(T_g\), and \(\Delta T\) exist only where every source
required by their definitions exists.
\end{itemize}

An absent source propagates \(\varnothing\). It is never encoded as zero,
\(\mathrm{NA}\), infinity, or a fictional payoff. Mechanical scripts check
hashes, schemas, finite identities, inequalities, and enumerated cells. They
do not prove PBE completeness, abstract measurability, universal
factorization, or the absence of unenumerated deviations; those conclusions
come from the textual proofs fixed by the source manifests.

## F.4 Causal scope and mandatory treatment {-}

\(T_g\) is a structural causal contrast inside the specified model. It is not
an empirically identified estimand for the WTO or another institution. The
treatment inserts an earlier and mandatory hegemonic proposal stage. Its
control starts at Round 1, so \(T_g\) includes the value of timing as specified
by the game. It does not describe an optional proposal right that \(H\) can
decline while retaining the same date-\(A\) payoff.

When a contrast is set-valued, each comparison is member-specific. A
selection-free claim requires the entire exact correspondence to lie on the
relevant side of the threshold. We do not promote the six later advisory
corollaries to frozen theorems. The exact result remains the source
correspondence and its declared domain.

This table is a rationalist reconstruction by the author, not a formal model
